qa.q: Study the imaginary lines of the Earth.

qa.a: A latitude measures the distance of a place north or south of the Equator, in degrees (°), from 0° to 90°.

qa.q: Name the five major lines of latitude and give their values.
qa.a: They are the Equator (0°), the Tropic of Cancer (23½° N), the Tropic of Capricorn (23½° S), the Arctic Circle (66½° N) and the Antarctic Circle (66½° S).

qa.q: Do latitudes meet? Are they all the same length?
qa.a: No. Latitudes are parallel and never meet. They become shorter towards the poles; the Equator is the longest.

sum.title: I. Latitudes
defs: A latitude (or parallel) is an imaginary line drawn around the Earth from west to east. It measures the distance of a place north or south of the Equator.
items: A. Major Lines of Latitude
– The Equator (0°) divides the Earth into the Northern and Southern Hemispheres.
– The Tropic of Cancer (23½° N) and the Tropic of Capricorn (23½° S).
– The Arctic Circle (66½° N) and the Antarctic Circle (66½° S).
– The North Pole (90° N) and the South Pole (90° S).
B. Characteristics
– Latitudes are parallel and never meet.
– They are complete circles that become smaller towards the poles.
– They go from 0° at the Equator to 90° at the poles.

qa.a: A longitude measures the distance of a place east or west of the Prime (Greenwich) Meridian, in degrees, from 0° to 180°.

qa.q: Name the two major lines of longitude.
qa.a: They are the Prime Meridian (0°), which passes through Greenwich in London, and the 180° meridian, near which the International Date Line runs.

qa.q: Give two differences between latitudes and longitudes.
qa.a: Latitudes are parallel and never meet, while longitudes meet at the poles. Latitudes have different lengths, while all longitudes have the same length.

sum.title: II. Longitudes
defs: A longitude (or meridian) is an imaginary line drawn from the North Pole to the South Pole. It measures the distance of a place east or west of the Prime Meridian.
items: A. Major Lines of Longitude
– The Prime (Greenwich) Meridian (0°) divides the Earth into the Eastern and Western Hemispheres.
– The 180° meridian is opposite the Prime Meridian. The International Date Line follows it.
B. Characteristics
– Longitudes meet at the North and South Poles.
– They are half-circles of the same length.
– They go from 0° to 180° east and 180° west.
C. Differences
– Latitudes run from west to east; longitudes run from north to south.
– Latitudes never meet; longitudes meet at the poles.
– Latitudes have different lengths; longitudes have the same length.
– Latitudes go up to 90°; longitudes go up to 180°.

qa.q: Garoua is at about 9° N and 13° E. What does this mean?
qa.a: Garoua is about 9 degrees north of the Equator and about 13 degrees east of the Prime Meridian.

qa.q: Which one do we write first: the latitude or the longitude?
qa.a: We always write the latitude first (N or S), and then the longitude (E or W). For example, Tokyo: 35° N, 139° E.

sum.title: III. Geographical Coordinates
defs: The geographical coordinates of a place are its latitude and its longitude. They give the exact position of the place on Earth.
items: How to Write Coordinates
– We write the latitude first, then the longitude.
– We always add the letter N or S, and E or W.
– Example: Garoua is at about 9° N, 13° E.
– Example: Yaoundé is at about 4° N, 11½° E.

evaluation: What is the difference between a latitude and a longitude?
A latitude measures the distance north or south of the Equator; a longitude measures the distance east or west of the Prime Meridian.
Which is the longest line of latitude?
The Equator is the longest line of latitude.
Garoua is at about 9° N, 13° E.
remediation: The line of latitude 0° is the ______.
The line of longitude 0° is the ______ Meridian.
The Tropic of Cancer is at ______ ° N.
In coordinates, we write the ______ first.
The latitude and longitude of a place are its geographical ______.
